DATA FORMATSFree

YAML to JSON converter

Convert YAML 1.2 to JSON, or switch to JSON to YAML. Paste a document or open a local UTF-8 file, inspect the result and download it. All conversion runs in your browser.

Local files & pasted text

Up to 1 million UTF-16 code units. UTF-8 files up to 2 MB. Nothing is uploaded.

TRY A COMPLETE EXAMPLE

Choose an example or convert your input.

Editing input or options clears the previous result. Convert again to apply changes.

A LITTLE CONTEXT

How to convert YAML to JSON

Paste one YAML document, select the JSON indentation and choose Convert. Mappings become objects and sequences become arrays. For the reverse direction, select JSON to YAML and provide strict JSON. Switching modes uses the last successful result as the next input.

YAML 1.2 core types ↔ JSON values

References: YAML 1.2.2 specification · YAML parser documentation · JSON: RFC 8259

Good to know

Which YAML version and types are supported?

This converter uses the YAML 1.2 core schema. true and false become booleans; yes, no, on and off remain strings. Dates such as 2026-11-27 remain strings. JSON supports strings, finite numbers, booleans, null, arrays and objects with string keys.

Are comments and formatting preserved?

No. Conversion preserves supported data values, not comments, key order in every case, quoting style or layout. JSON has no comments. Reverse conversion quotes string values so text such as "true" and "001" keeps its string type.

Can I convert anchors, aliases or multiple documents?

Bounded, noncyclic aliases can be expanded into repeated JSON values. Cycles, excessive alias expansion, YAML merge keys (<<), custom tags, YAML 1.1 directives and multiple documents are rejected. Expand merges and split document streams before converting.

Why are a duplicate key or numeric mapping key rejected?

Duplicate keys can hide a value that another parser would overwrite. They are rejected in both YAML and JSON. JSON object keys are strings, so quote numeric YAML keys. Complex mapping keys have no supported JSON representation.

What happens to large integers and decimal numbers?

Integers outside −9,007,199,254,740,991 through 9,007,199,254,740,991 are rejected; put exact IDs and larger integers in quotes. Decimal values use standard JavaScript number precision. Non-finite values such as .nan and .inf are rejected. Negative zero may normalize to zero in JSON.

What are the input and file limits?

Paste up to 1,000,000 UTF-16 code units or read a UTF-8 file up to 2,000,000 bytes, subject to the same text limit. Documents are limited to 80 nesting levels and 50,000 values and fields; output is limited to 3,000,000 characters. An initial UTF-8 BOM is treated as an encoding marker. Local .yaml, .yml, .json and .txt files are accepted; .yml and .yaml are alternate extensions, not different schemas. Empty YAML becomes null; empty JSON is invalid.

PRACTICAL REFERENCE

Check types before sharing configuration

The same-looking input can represent a different type. Quote values when their exact text matters.

YAML inputJSON valueReason
ready: true{"ready":true}Boolean
answer: yes{"answer":"yes"}YAML 1.2 core string
id: "001"{"id":"001"}Quoted identifier
date: 2026-11-27{"date":"2026-11-27"}Core schema does not resolve timestamps
items: [red, blue]{"items":["red","blue"]}Sequence to array

Conversion checks supported syntax and types; it does not validate a deployment configuration against an application-specific schema. For a worked comparison of types, comments and conversion losses, read YAML vs JSON. For tabular records, use CSV ↔ JSON. For a JSON string containing escaped newlines or quotes, use JSON unescape before converting the resulting document.
